title: Policy-driven GPU node profiles and IaC operator manifest
author: Arjun Patel
body:
Overview

This document defines a policy-driven approach for declaring and managing GPU node profiles (node classes) and the corresponding IaC operator manifest that provisions them across accounts and clusters. The goal is to standardize security, billing, and runtime settings for GPU nodes so higher-level schedulers and tenancy services can make deterministic placement decisions.

Goals
- Provide a minimal and verifiable spec for GPU node profiles (labels, taints, size, kernel build, driver, telemetry hooks, billing tags).
- Surface these profiles as a first-class resource in Terraform/Helm (operator) with safe defaults and canary rollout support.
- Automate cross-account policy enforcement: IAM instance profiles, egress routes, and VPC tags.
- Enable predictable cost attribution and fast recovery via snapshot policies and bootstrap manifests.

Scope
- Applies to managed GPU node pools used for inference and long-running tenant workloads (not ephemeral CI eval islands).
- Covers node profile authoring, Terraform operator manifest, validation tests, rollout steps, monitoring, and an incident checklist.

Owners and Contacts
- Primary owner: Infra - GPU Infrastructure (oncall: gpu-infra@redwood.ai)
- Author: Arjun Patel (infra-node-profiles)
- Reviewers: Sofia Martinez (security), Chen Wu (runtime)

Node profile model (concepts)
Each profile is a small JSON/YAML object with these fields. This section documents the canonical fields and expected values. The operator will reject profiles that fail schema validation.

- id: human-friendly short id (e.g. g1-standard-rtx6000)
- gpu_type: accelerator family (e.g. nvidia-a100s, nvidia-rtx6000, amd-mi250)
- vCPU: logical vCPU count per node (string or number)
- memory_gb: RAM size
- local_ssd_gb: ephemeral scratch space required
- driver_version: pinned driver/driver-operator version
- kernel_build_tag: kernel ABI tag to match golden image
- taints: list of kubernetes taints (string list)
- labels: map of labels (flattened into expected label keys for operator)
- billing_tags: list of billing labels to be attached on cloud resources and exported to billing pipeline
- iam_profile: cloud role/instance-profile name required to allow private registry and kms access
- egress_policy: enum {private-egress, nat-egress, restrict-https-only}
- snapshot_policy: snapshot schedule id for node image snapshots
- preflight_checks: list of test hooks to run after provisioning (e.g. kernel-compat, nvml-selftest)

Sample profile table (human-readable)
ID | GPU | vCPU | RAM | Driver | Egress | Billing tags
----------------------------------------------------------------
g1-standard-rtx6000 | nvidia-rtx6000 | 32 | 256GB | nvidia-525.60 | nat-egress | [team:core-infra, pool:dedicated]
g2-a100-32g | nvidia-a100s | 96 | 768GB | nvidia-535.86 | private-egress | [team:inference, pool:high-memory]

Operator manifest (conceptual)
The operator exposes a CRD called GPUNodeProfile and a controller that reconciles cloud resources (instance templates, node pool definitions) and cluster artifacts (taints/labels). The operator manifest below is a minimal Helm-values snippet used by the global infra Helm release.

```yaml
operator:
  enabled: true
  image: ghcr.io/redwood-infra/gpu-node-operator:stable-2026-01
  serviceAccount: gpu-node-operator-sa
  reconcileInterval: 60s
profiles:
  - id: g1-standard-rtx6000
    gpu_type: nvidia-rtx6000
    vCPU: 32
    memory_gb: 256
    driver_version: 525.60
    kernel_build_tag: rtx6000-5.15.0-kgeneric
    taints: ["gpu-only:NoSchedule"]
    labels: ["node-role/gpu=dedicated","env=production"]
    billing_tags: ["team=core-infra","pool=dedicated"]
    iam_profile: infra-gpu-node-role
    egress_policy: nat-egress
    snapshot_policy: daily-03-00
    preflight_checks: ["nvml", "kerncompat"]

  - id: g2-a100-32g
    gpu_type: nvidia-a100s
    vCPU: 96
    memory_gb: 768
    driver_version: 535.86
    kernel_build_tag: a100-6.1.0
    taints: ["gpu-highmem:NoSchedule"]
    labels: ["node-role/gpu=highmem","tier=infra-critical"]
    billing_tags: ["team=inference","pool=high-memory"]
    iam_profile: inference-a100-role
    egress_policy: private-egress
    snapshot_policy: hourly-01-00
    preflight_checks: ["nvml","device-link-check"]
```

Terraform interface (module contract)
The operator is configured via a Terraform module that manages the Helm release and cross-account bindings. The module declares these inputs (table) and guarantees outputs used by other modules. Represented here as expected variable names and output keys.

Required inputs (examples):
- helm_chart_version (string)
- operator_values_map (string: YAML blob)
- target_cluster_id (string)
- bootstrap_sa_email (string)
- iam_binding_prefix (string)
